content:
Sam: ran an nsys trace on the failing host, dropped nvtx markers next to the scheduler
Maria: nice — did you catch when the queue spike aligns with the KV sweep?
Sam: yes — around 1.18s there's a kernel switch (cutlass_matmul -> small_gemm) and queue time jumps ~28ms
Ben: can you paste the command you used? want to replicate
Sam: `nsys profile -o /tmp/run1 --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt python -u run_infer.py --workload microburst`
Sam: quick condensed timeline paste:
Sam: ```
# t(ms)  event
1150    dispatch small_gemm
1178    kernel switch
1206    queue wait spike +28ms
1235    matmul(lambda) quick exec
```
Li: that queue wait spike lines up with a KV cache sweep — batch of lookups missed cache
Dev-bot: artifact uploaded: gs://redwood-prod/traces/1713456789/nsys-run1.qz
Maria: cache hit rate dropped from 94% -> 62% over those microbatches
Ben: 62% is huge. are we seeing prefix eviction then rewarm thrash?
Sam: hypothesis: continuous batching window extended to 40ms to fold requests; that allows a KV sweep to interleave and cause prefetch/backpressure
Li: timeline shows prefetches firing at ~1160ms, they lock memory bus ~6ms and push CUDA dispatch latency
Maria: two quick experiments:
Maria: 1) shrink continuous batching window to 12ms
Maria: 2) force KV cache pinning for in-flight tail requests (avoid sweep)
Ben: I can A/B deploy those on staging
Ben: will add a perfetto label to overlay CPU prefetch timeline
Sam: also saw kernel variant flip — runtime picked a quantized kernel mid-run, increased per-token compute, reduced occupancy and increased queueing
Li: flip tied to seq-len estimation; executor re-evaluated kernel choice when KV misses increased effective context
Maria: numbers from staging: wide window (40ms) queue_time median=9ms p95=36ms; narrow (12ms) median=4ms p95=12ms
Sam: tradeoff: narrow window spawns more kernel invocations but reduces tail latency and KV churn
Ben: will run nsys with `--sample=cpu` and perf report to correlate memcpy and prefetch timings
Sam: repro steps I used:
Sam: ```
1) run workload seed=42
2) nsys profile -o /tmp/run1 --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt python -u run_infer.py --workload microburst
3) collect /tmp/kvcache-stats.log
4) tools/trace_viz.py --overlay-prefetch /tmp/run1.qz
```
Li: adding ticket INF-4523 (batching-kv-thump) with trace links
Dev-bot: created INF-4523 and attached gs://redwood-prod/traces/1713456789/nsys-run1.qz
Maria: next actions: Ben runs the two experiments, Sam will instrument kv stats at 1ms granularity, Li will add kernel-choice logging around re-eval
Ben: ETA for staging runs ~2h
Sam: leaving nsys snapshot and perfetto link in ticket :thumbsup:
Maria: if staging confirms, consider runtime patch to defer kernel re-eval until after KV sweep window
Ben: ack, will try a branch and report
Li: saw a small host memcpy stall at 1180ms correlating with prefetch
Sam: will include memcpy timeline in next upload
Maria: short summary: tune batch-window + kv pinning + avoid mid-batch kernel flip, prioritize latency SLOs
